frugal.et: Borrowed from French frugal, from Latin frugalis.

s: A lot of fruits are red.
harvest, crop, produce, particularly of cereal
Im August wird die Frucht des Feldes eingefahren.
In August, the harvest of the fields is brought in.
Frucht.et: From Middle High German fruht, vruht, from Old High German fruht, from Proto-West Germanic *fruhti (“fruit”). Cognate with Alemannic German Frucht, Hunsrik Frucht.

s: Gewöhnlich essen sie ihr Frühstück im Bett.
They usually have their breakfast in bed.
Frühstück.et: From Middle High German vrüestücke (14th c.). Equivalent to früh (“early”) + Stück (“piece”, here in the sense of “bite”).

früh.et: From Middle High German vrüe, vrüeje, from Old High German fruoi, from Proto-West Germanic *frō(ī) (“early”). Cognate with Dutch vroeg, German Low German fröh, Saterland Frisian fröier (“formerly”).

s: in the morning (general in morgen früh, otherwise regional, especially Eastern Germany, Southern Germany, Austria)
früh.et: From Middle High German vrüe, vrüeje, from Old High German fruoi, from Proto-West Germanic *frō(ī) (“early”). Cognate with Dutch vroeg, German Low German fröh, Saterland Frisian fröier (“formerly”).

to have something for breakfast (to eat as one's morning meal)

s: early waker, early bird (of male or unspecified sex)
Things were better in the past.
früher war mehr Lametta.et: Literally, “there used to be more tinsel [at Christmas]”, a catchphrase from the sketch Weihnachten bei Hoppenstedts (1978) by Loriot; itself probably a pun on the synonymous früher war alles besser.

s: prehuman (member of the genus Homo before Homo sapiens)
a bread roll to be eaten at breakfast
egg roll (food made by wrapping a combination of chopped vegetables, possibly meat, and sometimes noodles, in a sheet of dough, dipping the dough in egg or an egg wash, then deep frying it)

bouquet of spring flowers (bunch of spring flowers)
bouquet of spring flowers (bunch of spring flowers)
Nach gut einer Stunde wegen eines Frustfouls an Dominick Drexler bereits verwarnt, stoppte Uth vier Minuten vor Ende der Verlängerung den Ball klar mit der Hand.
a native or inhabitant of Frutigen
a surname transferred from the place name
in the morning, (especially) usually in the morning, every morning, mornings
Frühs esse ich immer ein hartgekochtes Ei.
I always eat a hard-boiled egg in the morning.
frühs.et: From früh (“early”) + -s (adverbial genitive), possibly continuing Frühs, genitive of obsolete Früh n.

s: A high-ranking person in an organization whose function is cosmetic or ceremonial in practice, having little actual influence on business decisions.
Der bisherige Chef der Verwaltungs-Oberleitung, Hirschberg, wurde in seinen Kompetenzen derartig beschränkt, daß er innerhalb des Konzerns nur noch als "Frühstücksdirektor" bezeichnet wird.
The head of the uppper management up to this point, Hirschberg, was limited in his authority to such a degree that he is now only referred to as a "breakfast director" within the company.

Wildes Drauflossparen, ohnr vorher Verdeckte Gewinnausschüttung eliminiert zu haben, ist ein orientierungslosen Unterfangen, mit dem sich in der Regel die Frühstücksdirektoren als solche zu erkennen ergeben.
Mad we-have-to-save-money measures without first having ruled out hidden profit distribution is an uncoordinated affair which, as a rule, has breakfast directors revealing themeselves as such.
Frühstücksdirektor.et: Frühstück + -s- + Direktor, literally "breakfast director", so named because hosting guests at mealtimes is stereotypically considered their most significant role. First attested in the first half of the 20th century.
